title: English Vocabulary in Use — Upper-intermediate (4th Edition) · Units 37–38
description: Curated B2 vocabulary, media collocations, reporting expressions, political institutions and election terminology, with original examples and Brazilian Portuguese translations.
sourceNotice: Prepared from the user-supplied book for personal study. Target words and expressions reflect the teaching pages and relevant exercises; all examples and explanatory notes are independently written. Original textbook passages, exercises and illustrations are not reproduced.

audit.scope: All teaching sections, the TV-schedule table, the UK and US government descriptions, usage boxes, exercises and relevant answer-key entries were checked for vocabulary coverage and distinctions.
audit.pronunciation: Selected broad British IPA for high-confidence words and short phrases; uncertain or long multi-word pronunciations are intentionally blank. Connected speech and regional variants are not exhaustively represented.
audit.languagePolicy: English only in all fields except Brazilian Portuguese glosses under pt.
audit.reviewMethod: Compared source teaching pages, tables, notes, exercises and answer key; independent example writing; reviewed translation, English patterns, provenance and offline JSON structure and audio targets. No live VocabLab import, browser text-to-speech or speech recognition test.
audit.limitations: No prerecorded audio is included. Browser audio and runtime app compatibility have not been tested. Political arrangements and technology naming may change from the 2017 textbook examples.

units.title: Unit 37 — The press and the media
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Upper-intermediate (4th Edition); printed pages 80–81 (PDF pages 81–82).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Upper-intermediate (4th Edition)
learningObjectives: Describe common genres of radio and television programmes and the people involved in them.
Distinguish subtitles, dubbing, streaming, catch-up services and different ways of distributing media.
Use natural newspaper vocabulary and distinguish tabloid reporting from in-depth journalism.
Use verbs such as investigate, broadcast, televise, shoot on location and be set in, and treat news as uncountable.

items.pt: programação de TV; guia de programas
items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: I checked the TV listings to see when the documentary would start.
items.note: A published schedule of programmes and their times.

items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: The actor spoke about her new film on a talk show.
items.note: Usually has a host who interviews guests.

items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: The host welcomed three guests onto the programme.
items.note: The person who leads a talk show; a presenter can lead other programme types too.

items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: Tonight's guest is a well-known novelist.
items.note: A person invited to appear on a show or to be interviewed.

items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: The children watched a cartoon after breakfast.
items.note: Here, an animated TV programme with drawn characters; cartoon also means a humorous drawing.

items.pt: programa de perguntas ou competições com prêmios
items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: The contestants won a holiday on the game show.
items.note: An entertainment programme where people compete for prizes.

items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: According to the weather forecast, heavy rain is expected tomorrow.
items.note: A report predicting future weather conditions.

items.pt: novela; série dramática de longa duração
items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: My grandmother follows the same soap opera every evening.
items.note: A continuing drama about a group of characters; often shortened to soap.

items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: That soap has been on television for decades.
items.note: Informal shortened form of soap opera in the television context; also means the cleaning product.

items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: The documentary examined how cities manage water supplies.
items.note: A factual film or programme exploring a real subject.

items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: The reporter investigated the causes of the accident.
items.note: To examine facts in order to discover what happened or why; a documentary can investigate a subject.

items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: The sitcom follows colleagues who share a small office.
items.note: Short for situation comedy; usually uses recurring characters and comic situations.

items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: They broadcast a sports programme after the football match.
items.note: A programme centred on sporting events, results or discussion.

items.pt: programa de atualidades; programa sobre assuntos políticos e sociais
items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: She watches a current affairs programme to follow public debates.
items.note: Focuses on news and ongoing political or social issues; British spelling programme.

items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: The presenter introduced the debate and invited questions.
items.note: Someone who introduces and guides a television or radio programme.

items.pt: série ou drama policial de investigação
items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: The detective drama is set in a small coastal town.
items.note: A fictional programme built around investigating crimes.

items.section: A · Radio, television and programme types
items.example: The final episode of the series will be shown on Friday.
items.note: One part of a continuing TV or radio series.

items.example: Social media and traditional media cover the event differently.
items.note: The usual collective term for TV, radio, newspapers and other channels of mass communication.

items.example: Television used to be a dominant part of the mass media.
items.note: Communication channels reaching large audiences; often shortened to the media.

items.example: I turned on English subtitles to follow the dialogue.
items.note: Written text showing speech on screen, sometimes translated.

items.example: The animated film was dubbed into Portuguese.
items.note: A dubbed film has replacement speech recorded in another language; compare subtitles.

items.example: The distributor decided to dub the film for younger viewers.
items.note: The verb describing the recording of replacement dialogue.

items.example: The old satellite dish is still fixed to the roof.
items.note: An aerial dish used for receiving signals from satellites.

items.pt: receber o sinal de um canal
items.example: Our antenna cannot receive that channel clearly.
items.note: Receive refers to obtaining a transmitted broadcast signal.

items.example: A local TV channel showed the town's celebrations.
items.note: An individual television service or station.

items.example: Several commercials appeared between the two programmes.
items.note: Especially in TV/radio, a paid advertisement; often plural commercials.

items.example: You can stream the interview on the broadcaster's website.
items.note: Verb for playing or delivering online audio or video without first downloading a complete file.

items.example: The station will broadcast the interview this evening.
items.note: As a verb, send a programme to an audience; also a noun meaning a transmission. Past: broadcast.

items.example: Archived radio broadcasts are available online.
items.note: Plural noun used for individual programmes or transmissions.

items.pt: TV sob demanda para assistir a programas já exibidos
items.example: We used catch-up TV to watch yesterday's programme.
items.note: A service allowing viewers to watch recently broadcast programmes later.

items.example: TV on demand lets viewers choose when to watch.
items.note: Content is available when the viewer requests it rather than only at a scheduled broadcast time.

items.pt: podcast; programa de áudio disponibilizado online
items.example: I listen to a history podcast on my way to work.
items.note: An online audio programme that can be streamed or downloaded.

items.example: Download a podcast before travelling without mobile data.
items.note: Download copies the recording to a device; contrast with stream.

items.example: Email remains an important means of communication in business.
items.note: Means takes -s even in the singular: a means of communication, not a mean of communication.

items.example: The news is on the radio at six.
items.note: Uncountable in this meaning: some news, a piece of news; use a singular verb.

items.example: The newspaper published an interview with the scientist.
items.note: A print or online publication containing reports and articles.

items.example: The tabloid newspaper devoted its front page to celebrity news.
items.note: The book contrasts sensational coverage with serious reporting; not every tabloid-sized paper has the same style.

items.pt: jornal de referência; jornal voltado a notícias aprofundadas
items.example: A quality newspaper may publish detailed analysis of public policy.
items.note: A textbook label for a newspaper oriented towards serious reporting and analysis.

items.example: The article focuses on housing costs in large cities.
items.note: Use focus on a subject, not focus in a subject.

items.pt: sensacionalismo; fato que causa grande comoção
items.example: The headline seemed designed to create a sensation.
items.note: In press contexts, something likely to attract strong public excitement; contrast with factual analysis.

items.example: The reporter avoided sensational language in the court report.
items.note: Sensational reporting may emphasise shock or excitement.

items.example: The paper has a separate page for celebrity news.
items.note: A common noun phrase for stories about famous people.

items.example: The financial scandal prompted a public investigation.
items.note: An incident that causes public shock or outrage, often involving wrongdoing.

items.example: She studied journalism before becoming a reporter.
items.note: The work of gathering, checking and presenting news.

items.example: The magazine published an in-depth article on coastal erosion.
items.note: In-depth means carefully and in considerable detail; the compound is hyphenated before a noun.

items.example: The paper carried an in-depth review of the new novel.
items.note: A detailed critical examination; the exercises specifically mention book reviews.

items.example: The headline did not accurately reflect the report.
items.note: The prominent title that introduces a news story.

items.example: The article encouraged political debate about public transport.
items.note: Political describes a discussion of government or public policy.

items.example: You can subscribe to a newspaper to access its digital edition.
items.note: Subscribe to is the verb pattern; a subscription is the paid arrangement.

items.example: Her digital subscription includes access to the newspaper archive.
items.note: A regular payment or membership giving continued access to a publication or service.

items.example: The network plans to televise the final live.
items.note: A relatively formal verb for showing an event on television; more conversational: show.

items.example: The director chose to shoot on location in the countryside.
items.note: For films and programmes, shoot or film on location means record in a real place rather than in a studio.

items.example: The detective series is set in Edinburgh in the 1990s.
items.note: Be set in introduces the story's place or time; it does not mean it was filmed there.

items.pt: publicar uma mensagem no Twitter (termo histórico)
items.example: The journalists tweeted updates during the 2017 conference.
items.note: A verb used in the 2017 source for publishing short messages on Twitter; the platform was subsequently renamed X.

items.example: The sports broadcast attracted a large national audience.
items.note: A sports event or programme carried by TV or radio; useful when discussing the replay of a match.

items.example: The channel showed a repeat of last week's match.
items.note: As a noun, a repeat is a programme broadcast again; the noun usually has first-syllable stress /ˈriːpiːt/.

sectionsChecked: A: TV listings, programmes, genres and footnote vocabulary
B: Broadcast formats, access, subtitles, dubbing and communications usage
C: Tabloids, quality newspapers and journalistic collocations
D: Media reporting and production verbs; common news mistake

units.title: Unit 38 — Politics and public institutions
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Upper-intermediate (4th Edition); printed pages 82–83 (PDF pages 83–84).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Upper-intermediate (4th Edition)
learningObjectives: Name and distinguish six forms or properties of government from the textbook.
Describe the main institutions, offices and legislative chambers in the US and UK examples.
Use election vocabulary and natural patterns for candidates, voting, seats and coalitions.
Distinguish policies from politics, majority from the largest share, and political word families such as govern/governor/government.

items.example: In a republic, political leaders are not hereditary monarchs.
items.note: The textbook describes government by representatives, generally with a president.

items.example: The country is a constitutional monarchy with an elected parliament.
items.note: A system with a king or queen as head of state; actual political powers vary.

items.example: The constitution divides responsibilities within the federation.
items.note: A union of political units under a central federal government.

items.example: Free elections are one important feature of a democracy.
items.note: A system in which people have political power directly or through elected representatives.

items.example: The dictatorship restricted political opposition.
items.note: A system of government in which power is concentrated under a dictator or small ruling group.

items.example: The territory celebrated its independence from foreign rule.
items.note: Political freedom from outside control; common pattern: gain independence from.

items.example: The islands became self-governing under the new agreement.
items.note: Able to run its own internal political affairs.

items.pt: representante; pessoa eleita ou designada para representar um grupo
items.example: Voters contacted their representative about the proposed law.
items.note: A person who speaks or acts for others; also an adjective meaning typical.

items.example: In a presidential system, the president usually has an independently defined term of office.
items.note: The book contrasts US presidential government with UK parliamentary government.

items.example: In a parliamentary system, the government normally depends on parliamentary support.
items.note: The textbook uses the United Kingdom as an example.

items.example: The president addressed the legislature at the start of the session.
items.note: Can mean head of state or head of an organisation; institutions vary by country.

items.example: The legislature debated the draft law for several hours.
items.note: The body responsible for making laws; Congress and Parliament are examples.

items.example: Congress held a public hearing on the proposal.
items.note: In the US system, the federal legislature made up of two houses.

items.example: The constitution sets out the duties of each branch of government.
items.note: In the US example, branches with separate powers are discussed.

items.pt: ser eleito; ser escolhida por votação
items.example: Members of the council are elected by local voters.
items.note: Passive pattern: be elected by a group or be elected to a position.

items.example: The mayor's term of office ends next year.
items.note: The period for which an elected or appointed official holds a position.

items.example: The committee will appoint a new director this month.
items.note: To select someone for a position, typically by authority rather than a public vote.

items.example: The party may nominate a candidate for the next election.
items.note: To formally propose a person for a job, honour or election; differs from appoint.

items.example: A government official explained the new procedure.
items.note: A person holding an official position, particularly in government.

items.example: The prime minister discussed the proposal with the cabinet.
items.note: The group of senior government ministers or advisers, depending on the system.

items.example: The cabinet minister answered questions about transport policy.
items.note: A senior government minister who is part of the cabinet.

items.example: The president nominated a candidate for a federal judgeship.
items.note: In the US example, a judge serving in the federal judiciary.

items.example: Several political parties supported the bill.
items.note: An organised group seeking political influence or elected office.

items.example: The majority party chose the committee chair.
items.note: The political party holding a majority in a legislature; the largest party does not always have an absolute majority.

items.example: The House of Representatives debated a new spending bill.
items.note: One of the two chambers of the US Congress; distinct from the Senate.

items.example: The Senate held a vote on the nomination.
items.note: The upper chamber of the US Congress in the example.

items.example: Parliament questioned ministers about the proposal.
items.note: In the UK example, the legislature consisting of the House of Commons and House of Lords.

items.example: The House of Commons debated education funding.
items.note: Elected chamber of the UK Parliament.

items.example: The House of Lords examined the proposed legislation.
items.note: The other chamber of the UK Parliament; its members are not elected in the same way as MPs.

items.example: Both chambers must examine the legislation.
items.note: One of the separate houses of a legislature.

items.example: The Prime Minister met party leaders after the debate.
items.note: Head of government in the UK parliamentary system described in the unit.

items.example: The head of government presented the annual programme.
items.note: The political leader responsible for directing the government; not always the head of state.

items.example: The prime minister will head the cabinet during the next term.
items.note: Here head is a verb meaning lead or be in charge of.

items.example: The minister will select advisers with relevant experience.
items.note: To choose from available people or options.

items.example: The parties agreed to form a coalition government.
items.note: A government supported or made up of more than one political party.

items.example: Neither party secured an overall majority in the chamber.
items.note: More than half of the seats, not simply the largest number of seats.

items.example: The MP met residents in her constituency.
items.note: A geographic area represented by a particular elected politician.

items.example: Each Member of Parliament represents a constituency.
items.note: Usually abbreviated MP in the UK; plural MPs.

items.example: The MP answered questions from local residents.
items.note: British abbreviation for Member of Parliament; read as two letter names.

items.example: The government announced the date of the next general election.
items.note: An election to choose members of a national legislature, especially in the UK example.

items.example: The politician met voters at the community centre.
items.note: A person active in politics, particularly one holding or seeking office.

items.example: Four candidates took part in the public debate.
items.note: A person seeking election or selection for a position.

items.example: She plans to stand for Parliament in the next election.
items.note: British verb pattern stand for Parliament or stand for election; in US English run for office is common.

items.example: He decided to run for office after several years of local campaigning.
items.note: Especially common in American English; equivalent in meaning to stand for political office.

items.pt: política pública; diretriz; proposta de ação
items.example: The party published a new policy on public transport.
items.note: A plan or principle guiding government or organisational action; not the same as politics.

items.example: She became interested in politics while at university.
items.note: The activity, debate and systems of government; contrast with an individual policy.

items.example: The polling stations opened early on polling day.
items.note: The day when the election vote takes place.

items.example: Voters went to the polling station before work.
items.note: A physical location where voters cast their votes.

items.example: Citizens can cast a vote at their assigned polling station.
items.note: Formal common verb–noun pairing; also cast one's vote.

items.example: Many young voters chose to vote for the independent candidate.
items.note: Pattern vote for a person or party; vote on a proposal means decide it by voting.

items.example: She marked the ballot paper and put it in the box.
items.note: The paper on which a voter records a choice in an election.

items.pt: assinalar com um X; marcar uma cruz
items.example: Follow the instructions before you mark a cross on the ballot paper.
items.note: One possible way of marking a ballot; the exact method varies between electoral systems.

items.example: The party won three more seats in Parliament.
items.note: In politics, an elected place in a legislature, not a chair.

items.pt: conquistar uma cadeira parlamentar; eleger-se para uma vaga
items.example: She hopes to win a seat in the next election.
items.note: An individual candidate wins a seat by being elected.

items.example: The proposal received a clear majority of the votes cast.
items.note: Often means more than half; the book also speaks of winning a seat, where electoral rules may allow a plurality.

items.pt: distrito eleitoral disputado; circunscrição com disputa acirrada
items.example: The parties campaigned heavily in a marginal seat.
items.note: A constituency where the likely winning margin is narrow.

items.example: She was elected to Parliament after a local campaign.
items.note: Pattern: be elected to Parliament; a person can also be elected MP for a constituency.

items.example: Voters had several candidates to choose from.
items.note: Choose from a range of options; the preposition stays at the end in the relative clause.

items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: A monarch may rule as a constitutional head of state.
items.note: As a verb, exercise authority; not always identical to govern, which can stress managing government.

items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: The ruler announced a new arrangement for local councils.
items.note: Person noun formed from rule.

items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: The coalition agreed on how to govern the country.
items.note: Verb relating to running and managing government.

items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: The governor signed the regional budget.
items.note: A person with executive authority over a region or state; position differs by country.

items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: The government introduced a proposal on road safety.
items.note: The institutions or people responsible for directing a country.

items.pt: presidir; dirigir uma reunião ou órgão
items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: The chair will preside over the committee meeting.
items.note: Fixed verb pattern preside over something; not necessarily to rule a country.

items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: The reform became a major issue during her presidency.
items.note: The office or period of service of a president.

items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: Elected members represent residents in their districts.
items.note: Verb corresponding to representative and representation.

items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: The group requested greater representation in the council.
items.note: The state or process of speaking and acting on behalf of others.

items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: Members elect a new chair every two years.
items.note: Verb whose related forms include election, elector and electorate.

items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: The election attracted a high level of public interest.
items.note: A formal process of choosing people by voting.

items.pt: eleitor; pessoa com direito a voto
items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: Each elector was given information about the voting procedure.
items.note: A person entitled to vote in an election; relatively formal.

items.section: D · Political word families and office
items.example: The survey asked the electorate about their main concerns.
items.note: Collective noun for all people entitled to vote in a particular election or area.

items.example: The ruling party announced its priorities for the next session.
items.note: The political party currently leading the government; not necessarily the only party with seats.

items.example: The chair was invited to preside at the opening session.
items.note: Usually used with over when introducing the body or meeting led.
